The airplanes bring people in. The people make them want to come back. ✈️💛

At South Carolina’s Triple Tree Fly-In, heavy September rain softened the main grass runway. Staff marked out a temporary runway on drier ground, and volunteers helped welcome arriving aircraft. Sunshine later allowed the regular runway to reopen.

In his October 13 firsthand report, pilot Jim Roberts describes the gathering’s familiar ingredients: airplanes, camping, shared meals and plenty of fellowship.

There’s a bigger purpose behind the fun. Revenue from visitors supports Triple Tree’s Aviation Centered Education programs, connecting young people with aviation through reading, seminars and flight-training scholarships.

Triple Tree’s own education program also offers mentorship that can take young aviators from a Piper Cub toward experience in a Stearman and Spartan Executive.

That’s general aviation at its best: a place to land, people who welcome you, and a path for the next generation to join in.

The fly-in took place September 21–27; the firsthand report was published October 13.
